title: Raghav Juyal Starts Shooting Any Body Can Dream as Franchise Lead
excerpt: More than a decade after ABCD 2, Raghav Juyal returns to Remo D'Souza's dance universe in the lead role he says he imagined 12 to 13 years ago.
body:
• Raghav Juyal has begun shooting Remo D'Souza's Any Body Can Dream in Mumbai, stepping into the lead role, he announced on Instagram on October 15.
  • Juyal was previously in the ensemble cast of ABCD 2, which starred Varun Dhawan and Shraddha Kapoor — he now leads the same dance franchise.
  • He described the project as the most important film of his career, saying he first imagined it 12 to 13 years ago.
  • His recent work includes the antagonist role in The Paradise, released September 24, with King, starring Shah Rukh Khan, due December 24 according to Pinkvilla.

Actor and dancer Raghav Juyal has started filming Any Body Can Dream, directed by Remo D'Souza, taking the lead role in a dance franchise he was once part of as an ensemble performer, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Juyal announced the start of the shoot on Instagram on Thursday, sharing a clapperboard photograph. Pinkvilla reported the same announcement and noted the gap since ABCD 2: more than a decade separates his ensemble turn alongside Varun Dhawan and Shraddha Kapoor from this return as the franchise lead.

"Today, I begin the most important film of my career. Not because it's the biggest, but because I saw it, dreamed of it, and lived it in my mind 12–13 years ago."

— Raghav Juyal, on Instagram

A full-circle casting

In his post, Juyal framed the film as a return to a world where he once watched from the sidelines. Now he is at the centre of it. He wrote that he intends to give the project everything he has and to deliver a dance performance unlike anything audiences have seen in the genre, signing off with the phrase "Zindagi Zindabaad." Industry colleagues including Remo D'Souza, Terence Lewis, Guneet Monga and casting director Mukesh Chhabra were among those reported to have congratulated him.

The arc is unusual in Hindi cinema. Dancers who enter film through ensemble choreography rarely move to sole lead in the same franchise. Juyal's path ran through television dance shows, comic and supporting film roles, and then a turn toward darker parts — most recently as the primary antagonist in The Paradise, the Nani-led action film directed by Srikanth Odela that released on September 24, 2026, according to Pinkvilla.

What is known about the film

Coverage so far confirms the director, the lead casting and the start of production, and little else. No release date, supporting cast list or plot details have been announced in the reports from Bollywood Hungama, Pinkvilla or the IANS and ANI wire versions of the story. The title itself extends the ABCD brand — Any Body Can Dance — into a new formulation, signalling continuity with D'Souza's dance-film universe while placing Juyal's personal story at its centre.

For diaspora viewers

Dance franchises travel well abroad because the set pieces need no translation, and Juyal has a large following among younger diaspora viewers who first saw him on televised dance competitions streamed outside India. When a release date is announced, diaspora audiences should expect the film in the usual US, Canadian, British and Gulf theatrical circuits for Hindi releases, with streaming details typically confirmed after the theatrical window.

What happens next

The shoot is under way, so casting additions, a first-look poster and a teaser are the next milestones to watch. Juyal's next screen appearance before this film is King, due December 24, 2026 according to Pinkvilla, which will keep him in front of audiences while Any Body Can Dream is in production.
